The '''46th Academy Awards''' were presented on Tuesday, April 2, 1974, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. The ceremonies were presided over by [[Burt Reynolds]], [[Diana Ross]], [[John Huston]], and [[David Niven]].

''[[The Sting]]'' won seven awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for [[George Roy Hill]]. ''[[The Exorcist]]'' and ''[[The Way We Were]]'' were the only other films to win multiple awards. [[Marvin Hamlisch]] won three awards, making him the [[List of people who have won multiple Academy Awards in a single year|third person to achieve this feat]] and, to date, the only person who has won three Oscars in one year without winning Best Picture. {{As of|2025}}, it is the most recent ceremony in which the three highest-grossing films of the year were nominated for Best Picture (''The Exorcist'', ''The Sting'' and ''American Graffiti'').

===Honorary Awards===
* To [[Henri Langlois]] for his devotion to the art of film, his massive contributions in preserving its past and his unswerving faith in its future.
* To [[Groucho Marx]] in recognition of his brilliant creativity and for the unequalled achievements of the ''[[Marx Brothers]]'' in the art of motion picture comedy.

* [[Lew Wasserman]]

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
* [[Lawrence Weingarten]]

==Streaking incident==
[[File:Robertopelpic2.jpg|thumb|Opel streaking during the Academy Awards ceremony in 1974, with host [[David Niven]]]]
During the awards ceremony a [[streaking|streaker]] named [[Robert Opel]] ran across the stage naked while flashing a [[peace sign]] with his hand. In response, host [[David Niven]] jokingly quipped, "Isn't it fascinating to think that probably the only laugh that man will ever get in his life is by stripping off and showing his shortcomings?"<ref name=The1970s>{{cite book | last =Boyer Sagert | first =Kelly | title =The 1970s| url =https://archive.org/details/s00sage | url-access =limited | publisher =[[Greenwood Publishing Group]] | year =2007 | pages =[https://archive.org/details/s00sage/page/n149 129]| isbn =978-0-313-33919-6}}</ref><ref name=AndTheStars>{{cite book | last =Frawley | first =Frawley | title =And the stars spoke back| publisher =[[Scarecrow Press]] | year =2004 | pages =224| isbn =0-8108-5157-1}}</ref><ref name="Oscars '73 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/846/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=847 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref> Terrence O'Flaherty, a columnist from [[San Francisco]], responded by saying that "there's only one trouble with streaking—the wrong people usually do it. The ones who should have removed their clothes were [[Cher Bono]], [[Twiggy]] and [[Elizabeth Taylor]]".<ref name="Oscars '73 Notes"/>

The incident would be referenced 50 years later during the [[96th Academy Awards]] in 2024; host [[Jimmy Kimmel]] brought up the streaker and asked the audience, "can you imagine a naked man at the Oscars today?" Eventually, a "nude" [[John Cena]], holding the award envelope for [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design|Best Costume Design]] over his [[crotch]], emerged from backstage.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fienberg |first1=Daniel |date=11 March 2024 |title=Critic's Notebook: Busy and Eclectic Oscars 2024 Telecast Delivers Many Highlights (and a Few Lowlights) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-reviews/2024-oscars-review-jimmy-kimmel-ryan-gosling-emma-stone-1235848832/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240311114431/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-reviews/2024-oscars-review-jimmy-kimmel-ryan-gosling-emma-stone-1235848832/ |archive-date=March 11, 2024 |access-date=11 March 2024 |work=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Naked John Cena pays tribute to 50th anniversary of Oscars streaker |url=https://ew.com/naked-john-cena-pays-tribute-to-50th-anniversary-of-oscars-streaker-8607065 |access-date=2024-03-11 |website=EW.com |language=en}}</ref>
